name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: A large-scale multilingual corpus for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, consisting of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and about 6K hours for other languages. The dataset is suitable for ASR and TTS research.
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. Preprint, December 22, 2020.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created from LibriVox audiobook audio and corresponding text sources, mostly from Project Gutenberg and other book websites. The authors downloaded audiobooks for 8 selected languages based on audiobook hours and text availability, downsampled audio from 48kHz to 16kHz, segmented long audio into 10-20 second clips using acoustic models and silence-based splitting, generated pseudo-labels with beam-search decoding, downloaded or manually retrieved source texts, normalized text, matched pseudo-labels to source text using TF-IDF retrieval and Smith-Waterman alignment, filtered candidate transcripts by WER, and created train, development, and test splits with no speaker overlap.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The training data is lower than the available audiobook data because the text source for some audiobooks may not have been downloaded, candidate labels may have been filtered during transcript retrieval, or data may have been filtered while creating validation/test splits.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read-speech audiobook audio from LibriVox and source text from Project Gutenberg and other domains including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, projekt-gutenberg.de, zeno.org, browser-copied text, and text extracted from PDF/EPUB files.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio was segmented into 10-20 second segments by running inference to obtain token timestamps and splitting at the midpoint of the longest silence between 10 and 20 seconds, or at 20 seconds if no silence was found. Source text was split into overlapping 1250-word documents with stride 1000. Candidate transcripts were retrieved by TF-IDF bigram similarity and Smith-Waterman alignment, then filtered out if WER with pseudo labels exceeded 40%. Numbers in matched text were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels, and heuristics were used to handle hyphens and apostrophes.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio data was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters such as punctuation, subscript/superscripts, emojis, and escape symbols, removal of end-of-line hyphenation, joining split word parts, and filtering characters outside a valid unicode range defined by each language orthography. Books with corrupted metadata, missing title, missing speaker or author information, multiple speakers, or duplicate versions were removed.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts were generated automatically by pseudo-label generation and transcript retrieval from source books. For high-quality development and test sets, human transcribers listened to the audio while viewing the transcript and corrected only clear and obvious errors they found.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports WER between generated transcripts and human rated transcripts for development and test sets to assess transcript quality. To avoid introducing potential bias from human transcription, transcribers were instructed to correct only clear and obvious errors.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Trained acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable Convolutions with ASG loss, wav2letter@anywhere for streaming inference, beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models, TF-IDF similarity retrieval, Smith-Waterman alignment, pdftotext, and a gender classifier based on SVM with RBF kernel.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, language model training data, pre-built language models, pretrained models, and training recipes will be made freely available at http://www.openslr.org and https://github.com/facebookresearch/wav2letter.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker gender was labeled for all speakers using a gender classifier. Speaker identity is also used for partitioning. The in-house data used to train segmentation acoustic models consisted of publicly shared user videos, but only audio was used and the data was completely de-identified.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors believe the dataset will promote open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR, and open new avenues in ASR and Text-to-Speech research.
rai:dataBiases: To avoid adding potential bias into the dataset from human transcribing, transcribers were asked to correct only clear and obvious errors. Development and test speakers were balanced in gender and duration. The dataset is based on read audiobooks, and English is the most dominant language in the source LibriVox data.
rai:dataLimitations: Training data is reduced relative to available audiobook hours because some text sources could not be downloaded, some candidate labels were filtered during transcript retrieval, and some data was filtered during split creation. Automatically extracting text for non-English audiobooks was challenging due to diverse domains and invalid or redirected links. The number replacement solution is not perfect because pseudo labels may not always have the correct transcription. Polish language model decoding is negatively impacted by a high OOV rate. The dataset is derived from read speech audiobooks.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for speech research, especially Automatic Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech research. It provides train, development, and test splits, as well as limited supervision training subsets of 10 hours, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets for low-resource training benchmarks. Development and test sets are intended for evaluation, and language model training data and pre-built language models are also released.
